_comment: AUTHORED fields of the heuristic registry. Names, detection tags and groups come from the vault note QUARRY - Heuristics Commons; fragment counts and confidence grades from QUARRY - Heuristics Illustrations. Both are read by code/heuristics_build.js, never copied here. This file is canonical for route, v6, gaps, join_on, rel, detector and note. No quiz content belongs in it.
assessed: 2026-10-28 against the nug-v6 prompt and schema (code/lib/burrs.js) and the measurements in code/lab/out/nug-v6/heuristic_gap.json

routes.join: found by a deterministic join on stored hooks (SQL)
routes.string: found by plain string code over titles, entity values or answers
routes.relation: needs a typed relation between claims; extraction (route a) and/or the judge (route b)
routes.judge: a pair that already shares a hook is recognised and labelled by the judge (route b); no extraction change
routes.card: describes the output shape or round shape, not a link
routes.author: needs the author or is out of scope

v6.covered: a nug-v6 burr already carries what the heuristic needs
v6.partial: carries part of it; see gaps

G1.title: Day-level date and date role
G1.fix: Deterministic scan of the claim text for day and month dates with a role cue (born, died, founded, opened, released and similar), stored beside the year hook. No model change.

G2.title: No typed relations between claims
G2.fix: Nuggetizer emits relation hooks from the draft vocabulary, each with a target string copied from the note and verified by code (route a, prompt v7); the judge also names the link class (route b).

G3.title: Loose hooks are not joinable
G3.fix: Canonicalise set, former-role, mechanism and uniqueness phrases into classes (embedding clustering with a deterministic join on the class id, or a closed vocabulary); try on a sample before any re-extraction.

G4.title: String layer not built
G4.fix: Deterministic detectors over titles, entity values and answers (checklist H3). No extraction change.

G5.title: News peg comes from the author
G5.fix: The author marks a note or burr as a news peg; the perishable flag is a different thing.

G6.title: Pattern and aside kinds are almost never emitted
G6.fix: Deterministic list and table detector for pattern burrs; a prompt change or second pass for asides; look at the vault's real list notes first.

1.note: Each hop is a cause or a name that hands off to the next; chains need typed edges to be walked.

2.note: Several effects of one event: join on the event entity; caused-by gives the direction.

3.note: Time hooks are years and decades; the same day needs a day-level date read from the claim.

4.note: Same role in different places: set or former-role hooks exist but rarely match exactly.

5.note: A local version of a foreign original.

6.note: Imitation or transmission hops, walked backwards.

7.note: Same name, different category: entity hooks carry a category since nug-v5.

8.note: A name that travelled; both ends are entity or place hooks but the direction is untyped.

9.note: The open-question field captures some why-questions but links nothing.

10.note: How something survives in a changed form.

11.note: A story that accounts for a practice or object.

12.note: Needs a news peg from the author; the perishable flag is not one.

13.note: A solution studied in one place and used in another.

14.note: A limit, accident or choice yields a famous trait.

15.note: The reason a discovery was ignored is the hook.

16.note: Join on the honoured figure; the channel (currency, mountain, award) needs the commemorates relation.

17.note: Two dated claims about one entity with opposite standing; the judge names the class.

18.note: A small act igniting a large consequence.

20.note: A biological property shaping a social or economic pattern.

21.note: The mechanism hook exists but is a free phrase; only named processes match.

23.note: Thin example; a label for the judge only until the author rules on it.

24.note: A behaviour once thought unique, found elsewhere; the uniqueness hook is a free phrase.

25.note: A surprising rule or protocol; recognised by the judge on a shared entity.

26.note: A real place or person shared with a work of fiction; entity categories (work, person, place) help.

27.note: Where a belief first appeared; burrs carry no source-of-claim field.

28.note: Two explanations plus a confidence flag; alternatives are in the design but not in the v6 burr.

29.note: Needs counts stored for lists; pattern burrs are almost absent.

30.note: A fixed element inside a fluid form; recognised on a shared entity.

31.note: A production choice and its consequence.

32.note: An explicit what-if; rare in notes, recognised on a shared event.

33.note: Weak example; judge label only until the author rules on it.

35.note: A small physical detail that carries the story.

36.note: First, only, extreme: the uniqueness hook is a free phrase, so exact joins almost never fire.

37.note: Streak, gap or count in a list or table; needs pattern burrs from a deterministic list and table detector.

38.note: Material hooks are the most joinable type; pair with an event entity.

39.note: A little-known achievement of a well-known person.

40.note: Shared school, kinship or epithet; the set and former-role phrases rarely match.

41.note: One entity with two contrasting properties.

42.note: An unrelated domain's convention used as the explanation; judge only.

43.note: The aside kind exists but is almost never emitted.

44.note: Looks-like pairings need images or the author's eye.

45.note: Etymon hooks and the etymology kind carry it.

46.note: The literal meaning of a name; an etymon hook, with the judge naming the class.

47.note: A digit, colour or material word inside an entity value.

48.note: Homonym hooks plus entity categories; knots keep the collisions.

49.note: One-letter-off pairs over titles and entity values.

50.note: A shared morpheme across paired names.

51.note: Initials, pun titles and backronyms over titles and answers.

52.note: The named person is not the original author.

53.note: A word that changed domain over time.

54.note: A name from a habit or deed.

55.note: The expected source is explicitly ruled out.

57.note: Old and new names are both entities; the rename direction is untyped.

58.note: Letters that concatenate, interleave or hide a word, over answers and titles.

59.note: One phrase used by unrelated entities.

60.note: Digits or dates recomposed into a title.

61.note: Many clues, one link; lateral sets and former roles are the free-phrase hooks that do not match.

62.note: Independent items and a withheld theme; the same hooks as Connect.

63.note: What it is plus the list it tops; the uniqueness phrase must match.

64.note: A description plus a cross-domain nudge; a card shape.

65.note: Weak example; clues ordered hard to easy is a presentation order.

66.note: Two or three sub-answers; a card shape.

67.note: A whole set organised by a theme; the author's choice.

68.note: A cross-set observation, not a per-question one.

70.note: The target spark-card shape: raw related facts plus is there a question in this.

71.note: Needs an image, audio or video; out of scope for a text vault.
